audit_name: NEXUS Phase 2.1 — ML Experiment Integrity & Reproducibility Audit

dataset_manifest.training_partition: 106 weeks (2010-02-05 to 2012-02-10) — 311,960 total rows (2,120 benchmark cohort rows)
dataset_manifest.validation_partition: 18 weeks (2012-02-17 to 2012-06-15) — 53,388 total rows (360 benchmark cohort rows)
dataset_manifest.test_partition: 19 weeks (2012-06-22 to 2012-10-26) — 56,222 total rows (380 benchmark cohort rows)

investigation_1_evaluation_protocol_cons.finding: The difference between Random Forest test WAPE 9.64% and 14.54% stems from two distinct, valid forecasting protocols: 1-Step Rolling vs Fixed-Origin Recursive Multi-Step.

protocol_a_rolling_one_step.definition: 1-Step-Ahead Rolling Horizon Forecasting with Weekly POS Lag Updates (h = 1 week)
protocol_a_rolling_one_step.operational_use_case: Weekly store inventory replenishment ordering after receiving Sunday point-of-sale realized figures.
protocol_a_rolling_one_step.feature_construction: sales_lag_1w uses realized ground-truth sales from week t-1 (available weekly at replenishment time).

protocol_b_recursive_multi_step.definition: Fixed-Origin Recursive Multi-Step Forecasting (h = 1..19 weeks ahead from origin T0 = 2012-06-15)
protocol_b_recursive_multi_step.operational_use_case: Quarterly open-to-buy merchandise budgeting and warehouse capacity planning conducted 4-5 months in advance with zero intermediate POS feedback.
protocol_b_recursive_multi_step.feature_construction: Intermediate test targets y(T0+1)..y(T0+19) are strictly withheld. Short lags (1w, 2w, 4w, 8w) and rolling statistics are dynamically populated using the model's own prior predictions. Long lag 52w uses pre-origin 2011 observations.

horizon_degradation_analysis.conclusion: A chronological split alone does NOT guarantee that multi-step forecasts are leakage-free. When realized weekly lags are withheld, compounding autoregressive error causes an expected 4.9% to 5.5% WAPE horizon degradation in tree models, and a massive 14.2% degradation in linear models. Tree models remain resilient due to pre-origin annual seasonal anchoring (lag 52w).

target_row_and_date_alignment.verification: Every single model generates predictions matching the exact shape, ordering, and (Store, Dept, Date) indices of the test partition in results/predictions_comparison.csv.

leaderboard_entry_count_explanation.explanation: Specification baseline 5 allowed 'SARIMAX or Prophet'. Because both Prophet and SARIMAX were successfully implemented, trained, and benchmarked per-series, both are transparently reported (Baseline 5A: Prophet, Baseline 5B: SARIMAX), yielding 6 baselines + 4 hybrids = 10 total entries.

leakage_prevention_verification.residual_models_audit: Prophet+XGBoost (Hybrid A) and SARIMAX+XGBoost (Hybrid B) compute base predictions and residuals strictly on the 106-week training partition. Residual XGBoost models are trained solely on in-sample residuals and never observe validation or test targets.
leakage_prevention_verification.time_aware_stacking_audit: TimeAwareStackingEnsemble (Hybrid C) uses TimeSeriesSplit expanding folds strictly within the 106-week training partition to generate out-of-fold meta-features. Ridge meta-regressor is fit exclusively on out-of-fold training predictions. Zero validation or test target leakage.

investigation_3_model_selection_and_vali.selection_protocol: Strictly on 18-week out-of-time validation partition (2012-02-17 to 2012-06-15) before observing test set outcomes.

validation_vs_test_divergence_analysis.test_winner: Baseline 4: XGBoost (9.41% Test WAPE) / Random Forest (9.64% Test WAPE)
validation_vs_test_divergence_analysis.reason_for_divergence: The 18-week validation window (Spring 2012) represents steady-state seasonal demand without volatile markdowns, where smooth harmonic Fourier curves fit tightly. The 19-week test window (Summer/Autumn 2012) introduced late-summer promotional markdowns and back-to-school surges, where non-linear decision tree splits adapt much faster to promotional markdowns than static Fourier curves.
validation_vs_test_divergence_analysis.academic_conclusion: The validation winner did NOT achieve the lowest error on the test set. Maintaining Prophet as the validation-selected model is scientifically honest; retroactively altering the selection based on test outcomes would constitute p-hacking and test set snooping.

investigation_4_prediction_intervals_and.model_evaluated: Hybrid D: Proposed Context-Aware Multi-Stage Hybrid
root_cause_diagnosis: 1. In-sample residual optimism bias: residual_std_calibration was estimated on in-sample training residuals, underestimating out-of-time test error variance.

2. Department-level variance heterogeneity: A single global residual standard deviation was applied across all departments. This caused interval bands to over-cover low-variance departments (Dept 1 achieved 100% PICP with excessively wide intervals), while severely under-covering high-variance departments (Dept 72 achieved only 40.0% PICP).
3. Heavy-tailed non-Gaussian error kurtosis: Using a Gaussian z-score multiplier (1.96) fails to cover leptokurtic retail sales outliers.
investigation_4_prediction_intervals_and.academic_recommendation: Do NOT claim that prediction intervals are calibrated. Transparently document that the intervals are uncalibrated heuristic uncertainty bounds with an empirical 72.1% coverage against a 95% nominal target.

investigation_5_reproducibility_and_veri.csv_to_json_metric_parity: VERIFIED (All recomputed MAE, RMSE, WAPE from results/predictions_comparison.csv match results/test_metrics.json with 0.0 discrepancy).
